key_risks.why_it_matters: Operating cash flow is negative in all three reported years while PAT trebled, meaning book profits are resting on receivables and work-in-progress that may never fully convert.
A 61% revenue CAGR with negative FCF in every year means continued growth requires continuous external funding; any funding squeeze stalls the model.
The prospectus itself flags low entry barriers and high competition, putting the 14.5% EBITDA margin at structural risk.

answers.question: check whether the growth is organic and repeatable
answers.answer: Partially supported: revenue grew from ₹18,828m to ₹48,782m in two years and the order book grew from ₹39,139 lakh (FY24) to ₹68,744 lakh (FY26) and further to ₹91,655 lakh by July 2026, which the company attributes to pre-qualification credentials and execution track record — consistent with organic, order-backed growth. But repeatability is unproven: growth consistently outruns cash generation, margins are thin, and the document itself calls the industry highly competitive with low entry barriers.

answers.question: veto — how is the business funded?
answers.answer: Not from operations. Operating cash flow is negative in all three years and FCF is negative throughout, so growth is funded externally. Reported borrowings are oddly near-zero/negative (₹232m latest), and net worth jumped from ₹7,702m to ₹15,678m in the latest year, implying equity infusions ahead of the IPO. The document extracts do not detail the funding sources directly, so the precise mix cannot be established from what was given.

answers.question: Our reading triggered a hard stop: negative operating cash flow in all three years. Is there an explanation in the document?
answers.answer: No. None of the provided extracts explain the negative operating cash flow. The risk and business passages discuss competition, order book growth, and insurance limits, but nothing about working capital absorption, receivable cycles, or why profits do not convert to cash. The hard stop stands on the evidence given.
